title: Calling a static method through a null object reference
answer: Java permits a static method to be invoked using an expression whose declared type contains that static method, even if the reference value is null, because the static method is resolved from the type and no object dereference is needed. The call can therefore execute without a `NullPointerException`. This style is misleading and should be avoided; call static methods with the class name so the class-level binding is explicit.
